1  ORDER I.A.No. 2631/2024, which is an application for dispensing with the service of respondent No. 1 and 2 is allowed at the risk of appellants.
With consent of the parties, heard finally.

Assailing the award dated 20/9/2019 passed by the Twelfth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in Claim Case No. 400246/2015, on the point of inadequacy of the compensation, the appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Learned Claims Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs. 4,48,000/- to the appellants/claimant for the death of one Nisha (daugther of appellants No. 1 and 2 and sister of appellant No. 3) in a road accident dated 14/5/2014.
2. The appellants had filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 45,20,000/- for the death of Nisha.
The reply to the claim petition was filed and after recording the evidence, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,48,000/- in total

; however, since Claims Tribunal found that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of Insurance Policy, the respondents No. 3 Insurance Company was exonerated from the liability and instead respondents No. 1 and 2/driver and owner of the offending vehicle were fastened with the liability, at the same time Insurance Company was directed to make the payment of compensation amount; however, right was reserved in its favour to recover the same from respondents No. 1 and 2.
3.

As the incident occurred, negligence of driver of driving the offending vehicle, the issue of liability jointly and severally to pay compensation have been decided recording the findings in favour of the appellant by the Tribunal and none of those findings have been assailed at the instance of the respondents i.e. owner, driver or insurance company
by filing the cross-appeal or the cross- objection, it is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail to burden the judgment on the said issues.
It is only the inadequacy of the compensation which has been assailed, however the arguments in detail have been considered in succeeding paragraphs.
4. As observed supra, it is a death case.

On 14/5/2014 when deceased Nisha was travelling in a bus to Gwalior, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of the bus driver, the bus turned turtle near village Katua due to which she alongwith other passengers sustained greivous injuries and succumbed to the same on spot, which gave rise to filing of claim petition by legal representatives (appellants herein) out of which this appeal arises seeking compensation for her death.
The case was contested by the respondents.
Parties adduced evidence.

The Claims Tribunal after recording evidence and hearing the parties, by impugned award partly allowed the claim petition filed by claimants and as stated supra, awarded a sum of Rs. 4,48,000/- break up of which is as under :-
Rs. 3,78,000/- Towards loss of dependency.
Rs. 15,000/- Towards love and affection Rs. 15000/- towards funeral expenses Rs.
15,000/- Towards loss of estate.

5 . Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the deceased was daughter of appellants no.1 and 2 and sister of appellant no.3.
Due to her death, the family suffered great mental agony.

It is contended that prior to death deceased was going private job and thereby used to earn Rs. 20,000/- per month and same has been duly proved through evidence even thereafter Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the notional income of the deceased including future prospect at Rs. 30,000/- per annum.

Even at that time the minimum income as per collector guideline was Rs.
8,400/- per month of a semi skilled labour.
Learned counsel for the appellants has further submits that the learned tribunal applying multiplier of 18 has assessed the compensation which is on the lower side.
It is further submitted that on other heads also amount awarded is on lower side.
It is submitted that the appeal filed by the appellants be allowed and the amount of compensation be enhanced.
6. None appeared on behalf of respondents No. 1 and 2 to contest the appeal even before the Claims Tribunal they remained ex parte.
Learned counsel for respondent No.3, submits that the amount awarded by learned Tribunal is just and proper and do not deserve any enhancement.
7. I have gone through the evidence adduced by the claimants.

After taking into consideration all the evidence on record, the amount awarded by the tribunal (so far as income of deceased and other heads) appears to be on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced.

Keeping in view the above,
the compensation awarded by learned tribunal deserves to be enhanced by Rs.2,00,000/-.

Hence,
the appellants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,48,000/- instead of Rs.4,48,000/-.
The enhanced amount of Rs.2,00,000/- shall carry interest @ 6% p.a.

The other conditions as imposed by claims Tribunal regarding breach of Insurance Policy, exoneration of Insurance Company and direction to Insurance Company to make the payment of compensation amount first to the claimants and thereafter recover the same from respondents No. 1 and 2, shall remain intact.
8. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award the appeal stands allowed in part.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
